title: Nine Miles of Asking
subtitle: 化学家与药剂师 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 化学家与药剂师（科学与技术·化学与医药）
meta: 主题语境：化学家与药剂师（科学与技术·化学与医药）　|　核心词汇：chemist　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chemist 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 my mother was sent to ask ① chemist she could not afford, and she said the asking was the whole of the lesson. The ② chemist, meaning the person and not the shop, was nine miles away and was asked by whoever came last; chemist, she said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ chemist in that town had the same counter, and the ④ chemist at the end, meaning the one the doctor kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked properly. Chemist, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ chemist was the whole of the prescription, meaning the science it carried and not the person. The ⑥ chemist, meaning the science and not any of that, is the only thing in a prescription that everybody trusts and nobody questions; chemist, he said, is either something you ask or the only word that means both a person and a science. She said the science is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ chemist had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the counter. The ⑧ chemist of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine miles and eleven years of asking; chemist, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ chemist I remember is the one at the end, which was asked in 1969 and is still described as the nearest in the county. A ⑩ chemist, my grandmother said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being asked; every chemist, she said, is a science that has agreed to look like a person. She said the science was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 药剂师；化学家
B. n. 药剂师（指那个人本身，与那间药房相对）
C. 固定搭配：ask a chemist 询问一位药剂师
D. n. 药剂师（指镇上每一位）
E. n. 药剂师（指末尾那一位）
F. n. 化学之学（抽象：它承载的那门学问）
G. n. 那门学问（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The chemist, meaning the person and not the shop
chemist was the whole of the prescription
the chemist had become a number in a report
The chemist of the whole thing
A chemist, my grandmother said in 1974

answers.why: ask a chemist 意为“询问一位药剂师”，1949 年母亲被派去询问她付不起钱的那位药剂师。
chemist 意为“药剂师、化学家”，指那个人本身而不是那间药房，在九英里外，由最后来的人询问。
chemist 指镇上每一位药剂师，每一位都是同样的柜台。
chemist 指末尾那一位（医生指定的那一位），是唯一有人认真询问过的。
chemist 意为“化学之学”，抽象指它承载的那门学问，父亲说 chemist 就是那张药方的全部。
chemist 为抽象用法，指那门学问本身，是一张药方里人人都信、却没人质疑的东西。
chemist 意为“药剂师、化学家”，到 1964 年这位 chemist 成了报告里的一个数字。
chemist 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英里和十一年的询问。
chemist 意为“药剂师”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1969 年询问过，至今仍被说成全县最近的。
chemist 为抽象总称，祖母说一位药剂师是唯一会因为被认真询问而变好的东西。
